summary: Full unsparing audit of utilityexplained.com's 12 highest-commercial-value pages (6 money + 6 flagship) completed per the operator prompt. Wrote 12 complete per-page entries in standard format (purpose/intent, quality N/10, seo N/10, weaknesses, ai_slop, visual_gaps, action + next steps) plus the slice-level monetization-trust judgment to .squad/SQ-065/wave1/lieutenant-pages.md (38,351 chars, verified: 12 entries, 12 verdicts, all four summary sections). All 12 markdown sources read in full; every internal link target mechanical-verified; affiliate/disclosure stack read at shortcode and policy level; two live renders spot-checked.
findings: MONETIZATION-TRUST VERDICT: TRUST HOLDING. Affiliate placements mostly help the reader (placed at decision moments, caveat-bearing, the monitor page even declines an unverifiable link: 'Sense is sold direct rather than through Amazon... no link here'); no unmarked affiliate links anywhere in the set; corruption risk is NOT in the affiliate mechanics, it is aggregate-promise arithmetic on the two biggest flagship pages.

Disclosures honest and visible, verified both in source and live render: affiliate-disclosure shortcode atop every audited money page (exists even on link-free 01); every product-box/inline link hard-coded rel=sponsored nofollow noopener with on-box note 'Price & availability shown on Amazon.com — we may earn a commission'; /affiliate-disclosure/ page specific, honest, and links editorial policy + methodology.

TOP FINDING: broken frontmatter on the revenue-core page — duplicate 'sources:' key at lines 8 and 19 of how-to-lower-electric-bill-complete-guide.md (grep-verified; page builds, silently keeping one block).

TOP FINDING: stacked-savings arithmetic on the same page — section banners (Save 10-25% + 15-30% + 25-60% + 20-35% + 10-20% + 5-15% + 10-25%) and checklist totals $50-150 + $50-100 + $100-200 = $200-$450/month against the page's own $164.88 national-average bill; two phantom-load tables on the same page disagree (game console $22-$30/yr vs $15-$25/yr; totals $75-$220/yr vs $50-$100/yr).

07-gas-bill-too-high: title says '10 Causes and Fixes' but body numbers 11 causes (grep-confirmed); heating share contradicts itself 40-50% vs 60-70% both tied to source [1]; furnace payback 5-8y (body) vs 3-8y (table) vs ~23y (its own worked example); sources mislabeled twice; uncited '15-30% year-over-year (U.S. EIA, 2026)' claim.

Cross-page claim drift: water-heater blanket savings ~25% (05) vs 5-10% (07) vs 4-7% (guide); EPA leak waste 9,400 (06) vs 10,000+/9,300 (point-sensor); 03's anchor promises the space-heater page 'compares units that deliver the same heat for fewer kWh' while 42's entire thesis is that no plug-in heater is more efficient than another.

Pages rated below 6/10: 50-best-smart-plugs-standby-power (SEO 5 — '50 best' slug on an anti-list workflow page, bait-and-switch vs 'Do not buy a plug because of a generic payback promise') and 05-how-to-lower-utility-bills (SEO 5 — H1 'Prioritize Improvements' vs siblings' '20+ Ways' anchor, mis-cited air-sealing row, cannibalized by the complete guide). No quality rating fell below 6.

Strongest pages: 42-best-energy-efficient-space-heater and do-home-energy-monitors-save-money (both 9/10 quality — anti-listicle honesty, DOE-anchored, declining weak links); point-sensor ladder and do-thermal-curtains (8/10) model decision-structure and tiered evidence sourcing (DOE 15% / AERC 5-16% / marketing 25-40% as Tier 1/2/3).

YMYL/consumer-risk language is the slice's best dimension: CPSC/NFPA/USFA fire statistics leading the heater page; 'Do not use a smart plug with a space heater'; gas-leak protocol ('Leave the house immediately... from outside'); monitor page's electrician-default panel install and fenced kill-list ('Medical devices, CPAP').
YMYL/consumer-risk language is the slice's strongest dimension; no dangerous override of manufacturer/agency guidance found in any of the 12 pages.

Internal-link hygiene is solid: 56 unique /blog/ targets across the 12 pages, zero unresolvable; but the two thinnest link profiles are exactly the two conversion pages (thermostats: 2 body links; 50-best: 4).
